title: Full faithfulness of a normalized ind-etale geometric-fibre component corner
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring, $f:U\to X$ a morphism of affine schemes whose map on global sections is ind-etale, $\Omega$ an algebraically closed field and $\eta:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ any morphism. Put $V=U\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. For every normalized component corner $c$ on $V$ [lem-zl-component-derived-pullback-square], the functor $c^*:D(\pi_0V,\Lambda)\to D(V,\Lambda)$ is fully faithful on ordinary unbounded derived categories, with the prescribed coefficient transport [def-zl-condensed-generic-scalar-model-data]. No genericity, irreducibility or nonemptiness is required here.

source.place: Theorem 4.13, diagram (4.4) and the paragraph following it

proof.text: base change makes the geometric fibre affine ind-etale over Omega. The geometric-field component-site comparison identifies its pro-etale topos with the profinite slice over its actual component space. The inverse image is the relative test inverse image specified by the corner's inverse_eq. Its absolute-test mate normalization identifies the coefficient comparison with pullback of Lambda. Consequently the corner's module functor is an equivalence: lift the inverse sheaf equivalence to modules using that coefficient isomorphism. It is additive and exact. Applying it termwise to complexes and localizing quasi-isomorphisms gives an equivalence of ordinary unbounded derived categories, hence full faithfulness. An empty fibre is included, with zero coefficient modules.
